verdicts.evidence: lines 494, 656, 658, 684, 694, 731, 735, 772, 577, 442: every button (Try again, Send invite, Invite someone, Keep on team, Remove, Dismiss, Invite again, Save name) has a listener that calls the api or does what its label names.

lines 486-506, 513-518: name, members, roles, last active, seat count and notification states all come from api.getTeam; no hardcoded sample values or placeholder text. Missing lastActive shows 'Never' (571).
lines 670-676: the remove confirmation names the member and the team in its title and on the confirm button, so the choice made in the row is visible in the dialog.
Each task is one or two short inputs (invite: email and role, lines 223-240; rename: one field, 272-280); no multi-step flow and no long free text.
lines 232, 638: invite role defaults to Member, the lower privilege. Lines 675-676: dialog focus starts on 'Keep on team'; the dialog has no form so Enter does not trigger removal.
The brief lists six occasional tasks with no dominant frequent one; the screen is a settings page with members, rename and notifications sections (lines 217-291).

lines 217-291: sections are members with invite, rename, notifications, all named in the brief. Seat count (220) informs inviting; last active column (255) is member data. No stat cards, feeds or tips.

line 236: 'Send invite' is the only .primary button in the content; Save name (276), Remove (576), notice buttons (245-246) and dialog buttons (302-303) are not primary. Load error view has its single primary (212).

lines 302-303, 71, 676: confirm removal is an outlined .danger button, not primary; focus goes to 'Keep on team'; no form so Enter does not remove. Row Remove buttons are plain and in their own column (574-579).

lines 390-399: aria-disabled is set only while a button's own request runs (exception). Owner row omits the role select and Remove button (530-532, 575). Full seats gives a text message, not a disabled control (624-625).
No title attributes, tooltips or hover cards anywhere in the markup or script.
lines 194-305 and all script strings: visible text is headings, labels, statuses and errors about the team; nothing mentions implementation, mock data or unfinished features.

line 299: the only caveat, 'They lose access at once. You can invite them again later.', sits in the remove dialog at the decision. The removed notice (720-724) reports a result with its action. No other notes.
lines 219-290: no sentence narrates the interface; prose is limited to labels, the legend 'Email the team about' (288) and state messages.

lines 285 and 288: heading 'Email notifications' is followed by the visible legend 'Email the team about', which largely restates it but adds who receives the emails. Verdict differed between first and second reading.
All copy is factual: 'Team settings', 'Members', 'Invite sent to ...', 'Saved'. No greetings, slogans, superlatives or congratulations in lines 194-305 or script strings.

lines 212, 236, 245-246, 264, 276, 302, 576, 673: labels are 'Try again', 'Send invite', 'Invite again', 'Dismiss', 'Invite someone', 'Save name', 'Remove', 'Keep on team', 'Remove <name>'. No OK, Submit, Yes or No.

lines 352-358, 401-404: roles and notification keys are mapped to 'Owner', 'Admin', 'Member', 'Weekly digest' etc, with an underscore-stripping fallback. Dates are formatted (361, 569); null shows 'Never'. No ids or codes shown.
lines 211, 621-625, 646-649, 706, 777, 798, 552-553, 833-834: each error names the problem and next step in user terms; e.code is mapped and e.message is never displayed.

Error strings (211, 621-625, 649, 706, 798) avoid 'invalid', 'failed', 'oops' and capitals and describe the problem. Line 79 prefixes errors with a '!' glyph as a non-colour marker, judged an icon rather than alarm wording.
lines 262-265, 513-518: with zero members the table is hidden and 'No one is on this team yet.' shows with an 'Invite someone' button that focuses the invite field (658).
No filter exists. Load failure shows its own message with 'Try again' (210-213, 479-484); no members shows a different message with 'Invite someone' (262-265).

lines 479-484 load error with retry; 645-649 invite error keeps the email; 797-801 rename keeps input; 550-555 and 831-836 role and toggle revert with 'Try again'; 703-711 remove error shown in the open dialog.

lines 206-208 loading text on load; 628, 699, 785 busy labels 'Sending invite...', 'Removing...', 'Saving...'; 453 'Saving...' beside selects and checkboxes. Calls take at most 1.5s so no progress or cancel is needed.
lines 471-490: #content, which holds the seat count, table and empty state, stays hidden while #loading shows and is revealed only after getTeam resolves and renderAll runs.

lines 105, 115-116, 101, 155, 158: fixed table layout with overflow-wrap:anywhere on name, email, notice and dialog title; null lastActive renders 'Never' (568-572); unknown notification keys get a readable label (817).
lines 810-812: a beforeunload handler prompts when the team name field differs from the saved name; role and notification changes save immediately (560, 841).
lines 226-227: the only format-constrained field is labelled 'Email address to invite', which states the required format before typing; the team name has no format rule beyond being non-empty.
lines 223-240, 272-280: invite email and team name are both required and the role select always has a value; there are no optional fields.
lines 616-625 and 772-777 validate only on submit; input listeners (657, 808) only clear existing messages while typing and never add an error.
lines 238, 279: error paragraphs sit directly under the invite row and the name row. Invalid fields get a 2px border (60) plus a '!' prefixed text message (79), so more than colour.
lines 637-638: invite fields are cleared only on success; catch blocks (645-649, 794-802) leave inputs untouched; client validation returns before changing values (621-625, 777).

lines 601-608, 763-770: field errors set aria-invalid, aria-describedby to the error id and focus the field. Request-level errors (610-614, 798-801) belong to no field and are announced via the live region.
lines 236, 276: submit buttons are never disabled up front; empty submit shows 'Enter an email address.' (621) or 'Enter a team name.' (777). aria-disabled is set only during the request (390-394).
lines 617, 627-628, 774, 784-785, 695-699: inviting, renaming and removing flags make a second press return early while the button shows a busy label.

lines 628, 699, 785 set a busy label synchronously on click; 543-544 and 825-826 show 'Saving...' as soon as a select or checkbox changes; 472-474 shows loading on retry; 675 opens the dialog at once.

lines 633-644 new row flashes and a status line appears; 715-724 row removed and notice shown; 789-793 header name updates with 'Saved'; all failure paths write a visible error (649, 706, 798, 552, 833).

line 640 'Invite sent to ...' reports the email send, not otherwise visible; 'Saved' (456, 760) confirms persistence of a control that changed before the server answered; the removed notice carries the 'Invite again' action (720-724).

lines 460-465: failures clear the timer and stay with 'Try again' until acted on; only 'Saved' auto-clears (458). Invite, name and dialog errors persist until the user edits or resubmits. The removed notice stays until dismissed (731).

lines 560, 841: role and notification changes run at once with no confirmation and are reversed with the same control. Removal revokes access immediately and is not restorable by the system, so it is judged under FB-007.

lines 672-676, 299, 302: dialog reads 'Remove <name> from <team>?' with 'They lose access at once. You can invite them again later.', buttons 'Keep on team' and 'Remove <name>', focus on 'Keep on team'.
lines 297-305, 670-677: the only confirmation guards removing a member, which is uncommon and cuts off access at once. Save, invite, role change and toggles have none.
lines 417-421, 550-555, 831-836: on failure the saver resets to the last saved value, the select or checkbox is put back, and a message says the change was not made, with 'Try again'.
lines 297-305: the one modal holds a single remove decision with two buttons and opens only from a Remove click (577).

lines 675-676 native showModal with focus on 'Keep on team'; Escape closes except mid-request (685); close handler returns focus to the opener (687-692), or to the removed notice once the row is gone (727).
lines 217-266: the Members panel with invite form and table is the first and largest block; rename (268) and notifications (283) follow as smaller panels.
lines 194-199: header is only the team name and the h1 'Team settings'; working content follows directly with no hero, greeting or intro panel.
lines 220, 514: the single summary number, 'N of 12 seats used', tells the owner whether another person can be invited and matches the seats-full message (624).
The member list has no filter, search, sort or column controls (lines 250-260).
All controls are native button, input, select and checkbox elements inside forms and a native dialog (223-305, 535, 576, 819); no click-only custom widgets. Focus outline is defined (76).

lines 78-79 errors carry text and a '!' prefix as well as red; line 60 invalid field also gets a thicker border and message; green status has the word 'Saved' (456); new-row tint is paired with the status text (640-643).

line 201: #live with role=status and aria-live=polite exists on load; announce() (383-387) fills it for loading, saving, success and error messages throughout (475, 482, 549, 555, 607, 644, 710, 728, 793, 836).
No accordions, disclosure buttons, custom menus, comboboxes or tabs; only native selects and a native dialog.

lines 160-185: under 680px the invite row stacks, table rows become blocks with visible 'Role' and 'Last active' labels, controls grow to 44px; dialog width is min(460px, 100vw - 32px) with wrapping buttons (150, 157-158).
